newsitem.title: CUBA: Bishops call for Cuban unity ahead of papal visit.
newsitem.headline: Bishops call for Cuban unity ahead of papal visit.

text.p: Cuba's Roman Catholic bishops urged Cubans on Friday to unite in a spirit of love ahead of Pope John Paul II's visit to the Communist-ruled island in January.

An Easter message by the bishops said the Cuban church hoped the pope's presence would "favor sincere and real unity in our church, among different religious faiths and among all Cubans, however they think."
The pope is due to visit Cuba on Jan. 21-25. It is the only Spanish-speaking Latin American country he has not visited.

The trip was agreed to at a historic first meeting between the pontiff and President Fidel Castro at the Vatican last November that underscored a recent climate of improved relations between the Communist authorities and the church.

The Cuban bishops have made love and reconciliation a message for some time as they press for more tolerance for religion and wider leeway for the church to operate in Cuba. Condemning intolerance in their Easter message, they said the church itself had historically been a culprit when it confused "unity with uniformity or with false unanimity."

Such an attitude gave rise in the past to "authoritarianism, the excesses of the Inquisition, intolerance, abuse of power and clericalism that have weighed so heavily on the memory of the church," they said.
The Easter message said reconciliation should be a central part of spiritual preparation for the papal visit.
